page: Microsoft Azure FX2mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance is configured with 42.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per core. It includes 118 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data highlights a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is highly competitive, with the Geekbench single-core score reaching 2355.0 and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression performing strongly. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores, fall into the weak to poor categories due to the physical single-core limitation. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is also relatively weak, though the Passmark memory score remains average.

From a resource density perspective, the FX2mds_v2 offers high memory capacity relative to its minimal compute footprint. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring large memory allocations without needing massive parallel processing power. However, the primary tradeoff is the low multi-core throughput and limited memory bandwidth for uncached large blocks, which restricts its utility for highly parallelized or compute-bound tasks.

This server is best suited for memory-bound, single-threaded applications, lightweight database operations, caching layers, or text processing tasks that benefit from a large memory footprint but do not scale across multiple CPU cores.
